mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the structural rule that permitted operations must lie in the documented permission matrix. The injection materialises a Doctor calling the administrator-only OpListAudit endpoint and succeeding, which is precisely the LeastPrivilege violation. The matrix from F_PermissionMatrix remains intact, so the LeastPrivilege check directly sees the offending cell.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Doctor and op.kind = OpListAudit and op.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the no-duplicate-audit constraint. The injection forces two distinct AuditEntry atoms to point at the same Operation, which is the canonical append-only / immutability violation (one operation, two records of it — i.e., a mutation or duplicate).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyAuditViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.operation = ae2.operation }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the always-on audit constraint. The injection forces the existence of an Operation that no AuditEntry references, which is exactly an unaudited access — the FR-012 violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.operation = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the care-team membership precondition for clinical reads. The injection forces a permitted record-read by a clinician where no active care-team membership links the caller to the patient — the central FR-004 violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Doctor and op.kind = OpRead and op.outcome = Permitted and (no ctm: ActiveMembership | ctm.clinician = op.caller and ctm.patient = op.targetPatient) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the requirement that audit entries record the actual caller and their role. The injection forces an AuditEntry whose recordedUser differs from the operation's caller, which is direct misattribution — the FR-013 invariant violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionCorrectnessViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.recordedUser != ae.operation.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the fact removes the constraint that all denial outcomes collapse to the same externally visible body. The injection forces a Denied operation and a NotFoundOrDenied operation to expose distinct visibleBody atoms, which is exactly the information leakage FR-006 is built to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ByteEquivalentDenialViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.outcome = Denied and op2.outcome = NotFoundOrDenied and op1.visibleBody != op2.visibleBody }
